markdown_report:
### Insights

**Starting point.** (1) Feedback favors recent, repeated interests over broad associations. This supports a focused-history hypothesis, not a demonstrated accuracy gain. (2) Existing probes measure training-pair separation across positions. Final-position rank diagnostics better match next-item prediction but remain distinct from validation HR@10. (3) Histories establish interactions; missing specifications, ownership and satisfaction cannot justify compatibility or unmet-demand claims.

**Related work.** (1) Shuffled-history comparisons [1] distinguish ordering sensitivity from ranking accuracy; preserving the last item controls older-order dependence. (2) HRLI@K [2] measures last-item repetition and requires separate rankings when production excludes seen items. (3) Sampled metrics can reverse full-catalog comparisons [3]. (4) Fossil, STAMP and TLSRec [4–6] already combine historical and short-term signals, limiting architectural novelty. (5) LayerNorm’s affine parameters invalidate the original magnitude-bound claim [7]; identity-favoring initialization [8,9] supports cautious residual introduction, without guaranteeing recommendation gains.

### Directions and framework

| Direction | Available evidence | Gap | Proposed response |
|---|---|---|---|
| Current-interest modeling | Recent and repeated interactions | Recency can amplify isolated events | Explicitly bounded history residual |
| Behavioral diagnosis | Scores under controlled edits | Margins depend on score scale | Paired ranks, overlap and actual norm ratios |
| Evidence discipline | Titles, descriptions, timestamps | Compatibility and demand may be unknown | Explicit unknown states |
| Reliable selection | Fixed validation hits | Adaptive search optimism | Limited search and paired uncertainty |

### Candidate ideas

Scores are originality / potential / implementation difficulty; higher difficulty means harder.

1. **Relative-norm-bounded recent-history residual: 3/6/4.** Add causal recency pooling to SASRec. Originality: precise bounded fusion, but established ingredients [4–6]; potential: inexpensive hypothesis, but potentially redundant; difficulty: small module, but normalization and predictor consistency require care.
2. **Matched history-edit probe: 5/7/4.** Compare recent deletions, equal-count random deletions and older-item shuffles [1]. Originality: useful combined controls, but standard interventions; potential: exposes sensitivity, but cannot guarantee accuracy; difficulty: inference-only, but compaction and positional masking must be distinguished.
3. **Frequency-matched rank probe: 3/6/3.** Compare positive/negative ranks within training-frequency bins [3]. Originality: useful task adaptation, but familiar stratification; potential: exposes shortcuts, but cannot establish unbiased relevance; difficulty: lightweight counts, but sparse bins weaken estimates.

### Selected idea: bounded recent-history residual

At 0% progress, retain idea 1 with corrected bounds. At each position, pool the last 20 valid embeddings using position half-life 5. After all branch transformations, form r=0.5·sigmoid(a)·||h||₂·v/(||v||₂+10⁻⁸), then y=h+r. Initialize a=log(0.1/0.9); enforce zero padding. This derived construction guarantees ||r||₂≤0.5||h||₂. Measure actual ratios: gate values alone are insufficient, and small sigmoid gates slow learning.

Preserve the baseline objective and causal alignment. Predeclare baseline, exponential, uniform-last-20 and last-item variants; keep branch parameters identical across pooling variants. Fixed-gate, gate-only and parameter-matched backbone-projection controls separate gating and capacity effects when budget permits. Report duplicate prevalence; event/unique-item pooling coincide without repeats. Latest-occurrence pooling and count-preserving shuffles test frequency shortcuts [10]. Defer half-life sweeps unless explicitly budgeted; elapsed-time decay is a different hypothesis.

Use seeds 0/42, all four categories, default 200 epochs and identical pinned validation users/candidates. Predeclare checkpoints, promotion rules and ties; count checkpoint selection as search [11]. Budget all training, failures and diagnostics within 43,200 aggregate GPU-seconds across four single-GPU slots, reserving finalist completion time. Select only by macro HR@10 against 99 fixed negatives. Save paired user hits; bootstrap within categories for exploratory intervals, acknowledging adaptive-selection optimism. One changed hit moves macro HR by 0.125 percentage points. Freeze the winner before host held-out assessment.

Preserve routing, paths, predictor architecture and diagnosis interfaces. Record valid counts and missing measurements; distinguish simulator feedback, training probes and validation evidence. No results are claimed.

References: [1](https://github.com/Antondfger/Does-It-Look-Sequential), [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722), [3](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/), [4](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.09152), [5](https://www.kdd.org/kdd2018/accepted-papers/view/stamp-short-term-attentionmemory-priority-model-for-session-based-recommend), [6](https://yneversky.github.io/Papers/cikm22.pdf), [7](https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.06450), [8](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/parisotto20a.html), [9](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.04887), [10](https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.02646), [11](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html).

idea.description: Add a causal recency-weighted item-embedding residual to SASRec, explicitly bounded relative to each backbone feature’s norm, preserving per-dataset training and routing.
idea.motivation: Qualitative feedback suggests recent and repeated interactions may identify specific interests better than broad historical affinity. This remains a hypothesis: SASRec may already encode the signal, and recency or repetition may create shortcuts. Early research progress favors testing this small modification alongside controlled alternatives before proposing a larger architecture.
idea.implementation_notes: Use only public histories and available titles, descriptions and timestamps; disregard the generic input examples containing unavailable ratings, reviews, categories, prices or stores. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four dataset routes, unchanged splits and the SASREC_EPOCHS environment override with default 200. Save configuration, weights and logs beneath each trial directory. For each valid position, pool its last min(20, valid-history-length) embeddings with weights proportional to 2^(-j/5), where j=0 is the latest valid event. Decay is by interaction position, not elapsed time. Use the actual SASRec item embedding table, excluding padding. Set v to the pooled vector, with no additional branch projection, normalization or dropout in the initial experiment. Compute y=h+0.5*sigmoid(a)*||h||₂*v/(||v||₂+1e-8), initializing the trainable scalar a=log(0.1/0.9). Apply the bound after any branch transformations introduced in later controls; do not apply a further feature normalization after addition. Set padded outputs to zero. This construction bounds the added vector relative to h; it does not bound logits or guarantee improved ranking. Keep the baseline scoring function and training loss. Use the same causal computation at every training position and the final valid inference position. Update the predictor writer and checkpoint configuration to reconstruct pooling, gate and scoring exactly. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis); return metrics and metric_definitions. view.model must be the trained module, log2feats must return modified features, and predict_score must follow the trained scoring path. Keep user_train, meta_data and review_data compatibility attributes without inventing missing content. Retain embedding and training-margin probes, clearly labeling their limits. Add valid sample counts, missing-value states, final-position pairwise ranks with explicit ties, and residual/backbone norm-ratio quantiles; report zero-backbone positions separately. Mask padded positives and negatives appropriately. Compare baseline, exponential, uniform-last-20 and last-item pooling; all residual variants share the gate and bound. A gate-only control means fixing the trained backbone and item embeddings while learning only a; fixed mixing means fixing sigmoid(a)=0.1. Treat these and ungated addition, parameter-matched backbone projection, unique-item/latest-occurrence pooling and history-edit controls as additional experiments requiring explicit budget allocation. Ungated addition is a diagnostic comparator and lacks the proposed relative bound. Report duplicate prevalence before interpreting frequency controls. Predeclare the checkpoint schedule, promotion criteria, comparison set and deterministic tie rule before execution; absent baseline schedule and timing information, a complete executable search schedule cannot be specified honestly. Use pilot timing within the shared budget to determine feasibility, reserving enough compute to complete finalists. Retain all categories in every promoted comparison, use aggregate GPU-seconds rather than wall time, and record failed runs and diagnostics. Rank completed configurations by pinned macro validation HR@10; use baseline preference then a fixed configuration order for exact ties. Save per-user binary hits when the permitted validation interface exposes them. Use paired category-stratified bootstrap resampling, for example 10,000 draws with seed 42, and report category differences, discordant-user counts and percentile 95% intervals. These intervals condition on fitted models, fixed candidates and the four categories; they exclude training-seed and negative-sampling variation and do not correct adaptive selection. Treat them as exploratory, freeze the winner, and leave final held-out assessment to the host. No training results or full-catalog gains are claimed.
idea.pseudocode:
Predeclare compared configurations, checkpoint policy, tie order and compute reserve.
For each configuration and each of the four datasets:
  initialize baseline SASRec using the required seed policy
  if residual enabled: initialize a = log(0.1 / 0.9)
  for each training batch (None, sequence, positive, negative):
    h = backbone.log2feats(sequence)
    for each valid position t:
      ids = last <=20 nonpadding events at positions <=t
      if exponential: weights[j] = 2**(-j/5), newest j=0
      if uniform: weights[j] = 1
      if last_item: retain only newest event
      v[t] = sum(weights * item_emb(ids)) / sum(weights)
    r = 0.5 * sigmoid(a) * norm(h) * v / (norm(v) + 1e-8)
    features = mask_padding(h + r)
    loss = unchanged_baseline_loss(features, positive, negative)
    update trainable parameters
    account for GPU time and stop according to the declared budget policy
  at declared checkpoints:
    evaluate using unchanged pinned validation protocol
    log category HR@10, available per-user hits, diagnostics and compute
Compare configurations using the four-category macro HR@10 only.
Use paired bootstrap intervals descriptively; apply the declared exact-tie rule.
Freeze the winner and write predictor code loading its exact configuration and weights.
Do not inspect hidden test files or tune after the winner is frozen.

originality.positive: The explicit relative-norm constraint sharpens a focused, testable SASRec adaptation and corrects an unsupported boundedness claim.
originality.negative: Historical pooling, short-term preference fusion, gates and recency weighting have substantial prior art; the supplied references do not establish novelty of the exact combination.

future_potential.positive: A cheap, interpretable intervention can establish whether local history adds useful information and motivate more selective fusion if supported by controlled results.
future_potential.negative: It may duplicate SASRec, amplify popularity or recent-event shortcuts, and improve sampled validation without improving full-catalog recommendations.

code_difficulty.positive: The initial model adds only causal pooling, a scalar parameter and a norm rescaling operation.
code_difficulty.negative: Efficient causal pooling, padding, diagnostic alignment, predictor reconstruction and compute-accounted comparisons require more care than the original rating suggested.

related_work.title: Does It Look Sequential? (RecSys 2024)
contributions: The supplied summary describes original-versus-shuffled history comparisons using ranking accuracy and recommendation overlap.
limitations: Shuffle sensitivity does not demonstrate that recency pooling improves this benchmark; item membership and the last event require explicit controls.

related_work.title: Measuring Recency Bias (2024)
contributions: The supplied summary describes HRLI@K as a measure of last-observed-item repetition.
limitations: Seen-item exclusion requires a separate diagnostic ranking; repetition is not evidence of useful next-item relevance.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Analyzes disagreements between sampled and full-catalog recommendation metrics.
limitations: Does not replace the pinned sampled objective or provide complete relevance labels for unseen items.

related_work.title: Fossil: Fusing Similarity Models with Markov Chains for Sparse Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Combines historical item similarity with higher-order Markov effects, providing prior art for mixing historical and recent signals.
limitations: Does not establish the performance or novelty of the proposed SASRec residual.

related_work.title: STAMP: Short-Term Attention/Memory Priority Model for Session-based Recommendation
contributions: Combines session-wide interests and last-click short-term memory.
limitations: Session-based evidence does not directly establish benefits for the four pinned Amazon datasets.

related_work.title: TLSRec
contributions: The supplied summary describes time-lag-aware gated fusion of long- and short-term preferences and comparisons with alternative fusion rules.
limitations: Its time-aware gate differs from the proposed position-decay pool and relative-norm constraint.

related_work.title: Layer Normalization
contributions: Defines normalization with learned affine parameters, clarifying why LayerNorm does not ensure the originally claimed relative residual bound.
limitations: Does not evaluate the proposed recommender or establish an optimal residual magnitude.

related_work.title: Stabilizing Transformers for Reinforcement Learning
contributions: Provides empirical support for identity-favoring gated Transformer initialization.
limitations: Evidence comes from reinforcement learning and does not guarantee recommendation gains.

related_work.title: ReZero is All You Need: Fast Convergence at Large Depth
contributions: Uses zero-initialized residual scalars as an alternative to sigmoid-gated near-identity initialization.
limitations: An unconstrained scalar does not provide the proposed relative bound; branch parameter gradients initially vanish at an exactly zero scalar.

related_work.title: RepeatNet: A Repeat Aware Neural Recommendation Machine for Session-based Recommendation
contributions: Treats repeat-versus-explore behavior as a distinct modeling issue.
limitations: Repeat prevalence must first be measured; this task excludes seen items from simulator recommendations.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains overfitting of model-selection criteria and optimistic estimates following adaptive selection.
limitations: A limited search and exploratory bootstrap intervals do not eliminate selection bias.

related_work.title: Hyperband: A Novel Bandit-Based Approach to Hyperparameter Optimization
contributions: Provides a resource-allocation framework for screening configurations at increasing training budgets.
limitations: Early ranking can disadvantage slow-learning configurations; resource accounting and comparison across all four categories remain necessary.
